sections.label: Turning everyday struggles into everyday skills
text: Turning everyday struggles into everyday skills

Occupational therapy for children focuses on the "occupations" that make up childhood — playing, learning, getting dressed, making friends, sitting still at the table, or coping with a noisy classroom. When these things feel harder than they should, it can affect confidence, behaviour and family lif

At Sensphere, our therapists look beyond the behaviour to understand the underlying sensory, motor, cognitive or emotional factors at play — and build a practical plan around your child's strengths, interests and goals.
Our approach is built on three things
Child-led, strengths-based practice — never a one-size-fits-all programme
Genuine partnership with parents, carers and school staff
Evidence-based tools, clearly explained in plain English
What is Occupational Therapy?

sections.label: Support for a wide range of needs
text: Support for a wide range of needs
We work with children and young people aged 2–18, whether or not they have a diagnosis, including those who are:
Sensory Processing Differences
Over- or under-sensitivity to sound, touch, movement or light that affects daily routines, sleep or eating.
Autism & ADHD
Individualised support for regulation, attention, transitions and sensory needs, at a pace that suits your child.
Coordination Difficulties (DCD/Dyspraxia)
Building gross and fine motor skills for PE, playground games, dressing and daily self-care tasks.
Fine Motor Skills & Handwriting
Pencil grip, letter formation, scissor skills and the strength and control needed for written work.
Emotional Regulation & Anxiety
Practical, sensory-informed strategies for meltdowns, shutdowns, anxiety and big feelings.
School Readiness & Transitions
Preparing for nursery, starting school, or moving between key stages with confidence and the right support in place.
Who We Help

sections.label: Assessment and therapy tailored to your child
text: Assessment and therapy tailored to your child
Every service can be delivered at our clinic, in your home, in school, or online — whatever works best for your family.
Initial OT Assessment
A comprehensive assessment combining standardised tools, clinical observation and information from you and your child's school, resulting in a clear written report.
1:1 Therapy Sessions
Regular, goal-focused sessions designed around your child's specific needs — building skills through play and meaningful activity.
School Consultation & Staff Training
Classroom observations, environment reviews and practical staff training so support continues consistently during the school day.
EHCP & Tribunal Reports
Independent occupational therapy reports to support EHC needs assessments, annual reviews and, where needed, SEND tribunals.
Sensory Circuits & Group Programmes
Small, friendly group sessions that build regulation, coordination and social skills alongside other children.
Parent & Carer Coaching
Practical strategies and coaching so the progress made in sessions carries through into everyday family life.

text: Getting started is simple

How It Works

sections.label: A trusted OT partner for your SEND team
text: A trusted OT partner for your SEND team
We work alongside SENCOs, teaching staff and pastoral teams to make sure occupational therapy recommendations translate into practical, sustainable classroom support — not just paperwork.
We're happy to attend review meetings, contribute to EHC needs assessments, and build long-term relationships with schools that want ongoing OT input for pupils across the year group.
What we offer schools
In-class observations and functional assessments
Staff training and INSET sessions on sensory processing and regulation
Sensory audits of classrooms and shared spaces
Contributions to EHC needs assessments and annual reviews
Termly consultation packages for ongoing SEND support
Sensory circuit set-up and staff coaching

sections.label: Experienced, HCPC-registered occupational therapists
text: Experienced, HCPC-registered occupational therapists

Sensphere was founded by a team of paediatric occupational therapists with backgrounds in NHS community services, mainstream and specialist schools. We believe every child deserves a therapist who takes the time to understand them as an individual, not just a diagnosis on a form.

All Sensphere therapists are registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), hold enhanced DBS checks, and engage in regular continuing professional development in sensory integration, DCD, and neurodevelopmental approaches.
Meet the Team
Sensory Integration Trained

sections.label: Common questions from families
text: Common questions from families
We work with children and young people from around 2 to 18 years old, and can extend support into early adulthood where continuity of care is needed.
No. Many families come to us before any diagnosis is in place. Our assessment looks at your child's functional skills and needs, regardless of whether they have a formal diagnosis.
Yes. We tailor the setting to what works best for your child — home, school, our clinic, or a combination — and we're happy to discuss travel availability for your area.
A typical initial assessment takes 60–90 minutes, followed by a written report within two to three weeks, including practical recommendations for home and school.
Yes. We provide independent occupational therapy reports to support EHC needs assessments, annual reviews, and tribunal proceedings where required.
Many parent coaching sessions, some follow-up appointments and school consultation meetings can be held online. We'll advise which parts of your child's care are best delivered in person.
We offer online appointments UK-wide, with in-person home, school and clinic visits available in and around our core service areas. Get in touch and we'll confirm availability for your postcode.
Simply fill in our enquiry form or email us to arrange a free 15-minute discovery call. We'll talk through your concerns and agree the best next step together.
